subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel managed active runs/background exec child processes, or preserve yielded/background exec sessions unless an explicit restart/process kill path is used?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves background exec sessions on tool-call abort and normal shutdown does not abort active runs, so a correct fix changes operator-visible lifecycle policy rather than just a local timeout.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Normal gateway stop rejects new work, bounds drains, cancels tracked managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog, and documents any explicitly preserved background class.

options.title: Preserve background jobs by default
options.body: Keep normal stop from killing yielded/background exec sessions and instead improve diagnostics plus operator-facing process kill guidance for dirty shutdowns.

options.title: Split by explicit mode
options.body: Keep compatibility as the default and add an owner-approved strict shutdown mode only after upgrade and documentation decisions are made.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Normal gateway stop rejects new work, bounds drains, cancels tracked managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog, and documents any explicitly preserved background class.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent shutdown fix and already distinguished this report from the websocket-close root cause in the issue discussion.
